traps.evidence: A brief first-person passage explains how seeing a medication near-miss led you into informatics, without patient identifiers or unnecessary clinical detail.
Any ward images, forms or dashboard examples should be prepared for public use, with patient and staff information removed and relevant publication permissions checked.
Label this as the reported result on one cardiac ward.
I would use your formal informatics title from the notes, rather than the LinkedIn “Clinical Informatics Lead” wording.
No hospital name or logo is proposed in the first reply.

swap.reason: The working-document concept and approach–projects–about structure could transfer unchanged to another nursing informatics portfolio, with different evidence.

backdrop.reason: Static diagrams and document comparisons carry the explanation; removing their depth, tilting and movement loses decoration.

depth.reason: The page assembles an introduction, approach, independent projects and biography rather than a developing story whose stages require their order.

clipart.reason: There is no single central object sustained through the scroll.

honesty.reason: The final plan accurately limits her title, distinguishes her contribution from the ward outcome and leaves unsupported claims unmade.

thirty_seconds.reason: The opening supplies her name and work, with direct links to project evidence and contact without requiring the full scroll.

plain_reader.reason: The opening supporting copy explains her nursing experience, workflow work and career goal clearly despite the abbreviated formal title.

judgement.summary: This is a thorough recruitment portfolio plan built around clinical documents, two well-attributed projects and accessible alternatives to animation. Its greatest weakness is that the documents decorate a conventional portfolio structure rather than forming a distinctive, developing story.
